subject: Architecture
title: The Beam Bridge: Simplest Span
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Beam Bridge: Simplest Span.

hook.text: A log across a stream is the oldest bridge on Earth. Every beam bridge works the same way.

buildup.text: A beam bridge rests on supports at each end. The deck pushes down, and the supports push up.

discovery.text: The longer the span, the thicker the beam must be — or it will sag and crack in the middle.

twist.text: Box girders solve this — hollow steel boxes are lighter than solid beams yet resist bending better.

climax.text: Most highway overpasses are beam bridges. They carry more vehicles daily than any other bridge type.

punchline.text: The simplest idea in engineering is still the most common bridge on Earth.

quiz.question: What limits the span of a basic beam bridge?
options: Wind forces pushing the bridge sideways
The beam sags and cracks if the span is too long
The supports cannot handle vibrations from traffic
